title: priority band collapse during cross-route batch merge causing transient per-key overallow
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Summary: Under sustained multi-tenant burst traffic we observed the rate limiting engine allowing low-priority per-key requests to consume credits that should have been reserved for higher-priority keys. The root is reproducible when the batch-merging path coalesces requests across routes/orgs and the priority metadata is lost or normalized incorrectly during merge, effectively collapsing weighted priority bands and producing transient overallow and billing misattribution.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy rate-engine-local with feature flag batch_merge_cross_route=true and synthetic load harness (tools/loadgen)
2) Create 3 API keys: key-A (priority=high), key-B (priority=low), key-C (priority=low) and assign them to same route with per-key window=60s and per-org cap=1200 tokens/min
3) Start steady stream of key-A at 5 qps and bursty streams of key-B and key-C that overlap window boundaries (see loadgen script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/priority-bands.sh),
4) Observe allowance counters on /metrics/rate_engine/allowance_per_key and per-route aggregate; look for allowance_B > configured cap and per-key debit misattribution in billing table
observed_behavior: - Low-priority keys (B/C) observed bursts that exceeded their per-key window allocation by up to 38% for 12-30s
- Per-route aggregate remained within limits but per-key debits were misattributed to the route/team rather than the originating key in the billing snapshot
- Logs show batch-merge operations that drop priority tags: 'merge_batches: src.meta.prio=nil dest.meta.prio=high'
- Post-failure: billing backfill required for affected customers to correct per-key charges
sample_logs: 2026-03-09T14:12:03.211Z [rate-engine] batch-merge id=0x7fa3 merge_batches src.key=key-B src.prio=low dest.key=shard-12 dest.prio=high
2026-03-09T14:12:03.212Z [rate-engine] WARNING: priority tag lost during merge; defaulting to route-priority
2026-03-09T14:12:03.213Z [billing] debit: amount=420 tokens charged_to=route-09 origin_key=key-B attributed_key=route-09
hypothesis: The batch merge routine is normalizing or overwriting per-request priority metadata when consolidating micro-batches across shard boundaries. Under cross-route consolidation the 'choose_priority' heuristic currently favors a single ticket-level priority and discards per-key weights, collapsing weighted fairness and enabling low-priority keys to consume headroom reserved for high-priority keys.
investigation_notes: - Added structured tracing to merge_batches and traced 47 occurrences where src.meta.* fields were nulled before accounting commit
- Unit test coverage for cross-shard merge existed but did not cover mixed-priority inputs; added new test cases in pkg/rate/merge_test.go
- Replayed production traffic in staging with sampling config and reproduced the delta in per-key allowance graphs (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/s/dashboards/rate_allowance)
- Temporary mitigation (deployed 2026-03-11): feature-flag batch_merge_cross_route=false rolled to 3 regions which reduced occurrences by 98%
- Found a code path in merge_batches that performs shallow copy of metadata and then mutates shared struct fields (merge_batches:line 287 in runtime repo).
